name: Aslan Ekman-Danso
role: Network intrusion and digital warfare specialist — netrunner
location: The Shelf — lower district tenements near the old lakeshore, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Aslan Ekman-Danso is tall and rawboned, the kind of frame that suggests either malnutrition or efficiency depending on the decade. At 25, scars map his face like a transit diagram of bad decisions and worse luck. The chrome is visible — reflex boosters wired into spinal column — shaves reaction time by 40ms — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. He works as a netrunner out of The Shelf, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Aslan Ekman-Danso operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.

core_fears: Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
core_desires: To matter to someone for who they are, not what they can do
Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
coping_mechanisms: Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
psychology.secret: Aslan Ekman-Danso killed someone who didn't deserve it on a job three years ago and has never told anyone. The face appears in dreams weekly.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Quiet and precise. Every word is measured. Silence does the heavy lifting.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Repeats the last thing someone said back to them before responding — processing or intimidation
Whispers when angry — the quieter the voice, the worse the situation
example_lines: "Every system has a door. Most of them have a door the architect forgot about."
"I don't hack networks. I have conversations with them. Most of them are lonely."
"The ice they're running is military-grade. That means expensive, not impenetrable."

story_hooks: Aslan Ekman-Danso intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Aslan Ekman-Danso's reputation — and a price for silence
A Tier 4 executive offers Aslan Ekman-Danso a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
narrative_function: Aslan Ekman-Danso functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Reflex boosters wired into spinal column — shaves reaction time by 40ms. Hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.

strengths: photographic memory for faces and layouts
ability to remain calm under fire
weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
habits: Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Practices a kata or fighting form every morning regardless of circumstances
Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
breaking_points: Their body rejecting their cyberware — chrome rot, immune rejection, the nightmare scenario
Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
